projects.teaser: A multi-sensor remote sensing and spatial impact assessment using Sentinel-2 Surface Reflectance in Google Earth Engine and ArcMap. The project isolates inundation extent and vegetation loss across the Chenab River floodplain (Gujrat–Sialkot) following the 2025 monsoon flood event.
projects.problem: Monsoonal flooding along the Chenab River in Punjab, Pakistan regularly inflicts severe damage on agricultural croplands and rural infrastructure. Following the 2025 flood event, local authorities required a rapid, quantitative assessment to distinguish direct standing floodwaters from broader crop degradation and waterlogging in low-lying agricultural zones between Gujrat and Sialkot districts.
projects.solution:
`Developed a dual-index satellite change-detection workflow using Sentinel-2 Level-2A imagery inside Google Earth Engine and ArcMap:

• Cloud Masking & Processing: Filtered multi-temporal imagery using Scene Classification Layer (SCL) masks to build 10m cloud-free pre-flood (May–June) and post-flood (Sept–Oct) median composites.
• Spectral Index Computation: Derived NDVI (vegetation vigor) and MNDWI (surface wetness/water) rasters to isolate surface changes.
• Impact Matrix Modeling: Combined thresholded binary masks (MNDWI > 0.2 for standing water; ΔNDVI < -0.2 for vegetation loss) via map algebra: Impact = (Flooded * 2) + Veg_Loss.
• Spatial Quantification: Classified 1,414.78 km² total land area into 4 distinct operational impact zones, accurately isolating 169.45 km² of high-impact severely damaged cropland, 517.83 km² of active inundation, and 91.44 km² of waterlogged crop degradation.`
projects.title: Flood Impact Vegetation Damage Assessment Chenab River 2025
